sources.fullCitation: Jan Kiepura with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester conducted by Dr. Weissmann. “Oh Madonna!”, from Ein Lied für dich; label credits music to B. Kaper and Walter Jurmann and words to Fritz Rotter and Ernst Marischka. Odeon O-4707 a, matrix Be 10220, take 2; recorded 11 February 1933. Disc label photograph and audio transfer published by the Great 78 Project, Internet Archive.
sources.title: Oh Madonna! — Odeon O-4707 a
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura; Odeon Künstler-Orchester
sources.researchNote: The photograph identifies Odeon O-4707 a, matrix Be 10220, and the runout shows take 2. Christian Zwarg’s Odeon matrix discography lists Be 10220-2 under 11 February 1933, Berlin, Schlesische Straße 26, room 2, with Jan Kiepura and Frieder Weissmann. The indexed PDF text was consulted; the complete file could not be retrieved during this review. Internet Archive instead supplies 1932 without a stated basis; that year conflicts with the matrix chronology and is not adopted. The structured date describes the recording session, not the issue or manufacture of this copy. Henry König’s Odeon label list separately lists O-4707 under 1933 but leaves the release-date column empty. The label does not identify Wiener Boheme-Verlag as the sheet-music publisher.

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11811, “Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo”
sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers. “Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo.” Paso doble. YouTube transfer published by jonjamg; the description identifies Odeon O-11811, matrix Be 10227, and accompaniment by the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt. The catalogue issue is dated April 1933 in Henry König’s Odeon label list.
sources.title: Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo — Odeon O-11811
sources.creator: Hans Albers, with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt
sources.researchNote: Henry König’s Odeon label list identifies Hans Albers, Odeon O-11811, matrix Be 10227-2, a session in Berlin, room 2, on 13 February 1933, and release in April 1933. The upload description gives Be 10227 without a take suffix; its matrix number must not be silently expanded to take 2. The label is not shown in the consulted upload material, and its identification of the orchestra and Otto Dobrindt remains uploader-supplied. The filmed label of the coupled title in SRC0699 identifies the orchestra and conductor for that side; it is not direct label evidence for this performance. The structured date describes the catalogue issue, not the recording session or manufacture of the transferred copy.

additionalLinks.label: Henry König, Odeon label list — O-11811, Be 10227-2

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11811 a, “Immer wenn ich glücklich bin”
sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt. “Immer wenn ich glücklich bin.” Foxtrot from Heut’ kommt’s drauf an; label credits music to Walter Jurmann and B. Kaper and words to Fritz Rotter. Odeon O-11811 a, matrix Be 10226; issued April 1933. Filmed-label transfer published by Schellackplatte on YouTube.
sources.title: Immer wenn ich glücklich bin — Odeon O-11811 a
sources.creator: Hans Albers; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, Otto Dobrindt, conductor
sources.researchNote: The video’s label identifies Hans Albers, the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt, O-11811 a and Be 10226. Henry König’s Odeon label list independently documents the session in Berlin, room 2, on 13 February 1933 and the issue in April 1933, citing Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst, vol. 1. The structured date describes that issue, not the February session. The companion title, “Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo”, is catalogued as Be 10227-2 and documented at SRC0697. The filmed copy carries a C. A. Klemm dealer sticker and a notice prohibiting radio transmission without permission.

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11439 a, “Ich weiß ein kleines Café”
sources.fullCitation: Austin Egen, accompanied by the Odeon-Tango-Orchester. “Ich weiß ein kleines Café.” Tango; label credits Dr. B. Kaper and Austin Egen, with words by Fritz Rotter. Odeon O-11439 a, matrix Be 9409; issued May 1931. Label filmed in the YouTube upload by Ilja Livschakoff.
sources.title: Ich weiß ein kleines Café — Odeon O-11439 a
sources.creator: Austin Egen; Odeon-Tango-Orchester
sources.researchNote: Wolfgang Stanicek’s dissertation Austin Egen (2010), p. 156, lists Odeon O-11439a, matrix Be 9409, with Austin Egen and the Odeon-Tango-Orchester: “NE 05/1931” and a Berlin session on 12 March 1931, citing Weihermüller’s Egen discography, p. 380. The structured date describes the May 1931 issue, not the March session. The label in the transfer independently matches the catalogue number, matrix and performers; it also prints “Auch als Tanzplatte geeignet”, B.I.E.M. and Carl Lindström A.-G.

sources.fullCitation: Jan Kiepura with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Dr. Weissmann. “Ninon”, from Ein Lied für dich; music by Walter Jurmann and Dr. Bronislaw Kaper, words by Fritz Rotter and Ernst Marischka. sources.title: Ninon — Jan Kiepura, YouTube
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, Dr. Weissmann, conductor

Odeon, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Signorina, ich liebe dich — Odeon
sources.creator: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, Gesang: Luigi Bernauer, auf dem Etikett als Fred Lustig angegeben
sources.researchNote: The uploader dates the issue to 1932 and associates the side with Hochzeitsreise zu dritt. The Odeon label list identifies the matching title and performers as O-11768, side B, matrix Be 10147, with 1933 in its general year column; its separate release-date column is empty. The filmed label carries no year. The structured date retains the uploader’s 1932 as disputed, not confirmed: the catalogue’s 1933 does not by itself establish a precise issue or session date.

sources.shortCitation: YouTube, Dajos Béla, “Du liebst mich nicht mehr”
sources.fullCitation: “Du liebst mich nicht mehr.” Slow-fox. YouTube transfer published by Radiomuseum Hardthausen; the uploader identifies Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, reports a Berlin recording in 1932 and gives the music credit “Bob Henders”.
sources.title: Du liebst mich nicht mehr — Dajos Béla, YouTube
sources.creator: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla
sources.researchNote: The upload reports a music credit to Bob Henders, a Berlin recording in 1932 and an Odeon first issue, but supplies no catalogue or matrix number. It shows a portrait from a Funk-Almanach rather than the label. Henry König’s Odeon label list separately documents this title with Dajos Béla as O-11667, Be 9946, recorded on 10 June 1932 in Berlin, Schlesische Straße 26, room 4; the release-date column is empty. The same list also assigns Be 9946 to the different title “Heute Nacht oder nie!”, an unresolved matrix inconsistency. The upload has not been matched to a verified pressing or take; neither O-11667 nor the exact session date is assigned to it. The structured year remains the uploader-reported recording year, not a confirmed issue date. The name Bob Henders in these recording descriptions does not by itself resolve the work’s authorship.

works.sortTitle: Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo
works.publicNote: The lyric is signed “P. Kuckuck”. Behind the name stood Fritz Rotter, who is credited with the film’s lyrics and who wrote its two other songs under his own name, on prints where Kaper and Jurmann appeared as “Ernst Martin”; the publisher’s house history states that Rotter signed this one number under the pseudonym, in the year all three had to leave Germany. GEMA and the Library of Congress still register Peter Kuckuck as a name of its own.
